title: A read / response DTO never exposes a credential-shaped field
intent: Routes serialize a response DTO out of the boundary, so a field whose name reads like a secret -- ``password`` / ``hashed_password`` / ``*secret`` / ``*api_key`` / ``*token`` -- would leak the credential to every caller. A response DTO is a ``BaseSchema`` / ``BaseUpdateSchema`` model **or** any class wired as a ``response_model=`` (so an input ``*Create`` / ``*Update`` mistakenly reused as a response is caught), excluding the inputs that are only ever request bodies (a client *supplies* a password) and ``table=True`` models (a table may store the hash). Plain helper classes are not policed. This guards the gap ``response_model_not_table_model`` leaves: a hand-rolled Read model that copies the stored hash. (``token_version`` / ``version`` are integer counters, not secrets.)

enforcement.ref: standard: responses never expose credential-shaped fields

runtime.rationale: A boot-time scan of each route's declared response DTO fields could refuse credential-shaped names on the composition seam _validate_router_response_models already owns, with the same cross-package fidelity; it is not shipped. The black-box probe observes a running app but is a conformance-suite check, not an in-app fail-closed control.
